summary: Anthropic announced an expanded agreement with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU compute capacity expected online starting 2027, alongside disclosure that run-rate revenue has grown from about $9 billion to over $30 billion.

mechanisms.reason: A multi-gigawatt commitment of new TPU capacity directly expands training and serving infrastructure for frontier Claude models.
mechanisms.quote: We have signed a new agreement with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity that we expect to come online starting in 2027.

mechanisms.reason: Multiple gigawatts of new compute capacity sited largely in the US implies a corresponding large increase in datacentre power demand.
mechanisms.quote: The vast majority of the new compute will be sited in the United States, making this partnership a major expansion of our November 2025 commitment to invest $50 billion in strengthening American computing infrastructure.

mechanisms.reason: Disclosed run-rate revenue growth from ~$9B to over $30B and a doubling of customers spending over $1M annually indicate surging inference usage driving the need for more capacity.
mechanisms.quote: Our run-rate revenue has now surpassed $30 billion—up from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025.

categories.reason: Google Cloud is deepening its TPU supply relationship with Anthropic, expanding a hyperscale platform's role in frontier AI compute.
categories.quote: The partnership deepens our existing work with Google Cloud—building on the increased TPU capacity we announced last October—as well as our relationship with Broadcom.

categories.reason: Broadcom, as co-designer/supplier of custom TPU silicon, benefits directly from this multi-gigawatt capacity expansion.
categories.quote: We have signed a new agreement with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity that we expect to come online starting in 2027.

notable_reason: A disclosed multi-gigawatt compute commitment alongside revenue tripling to over $30 billion run-rate is a major, quantified signal of accelerating AI infrastructure demand.
